question.leadin: Answer the following about weird Chinese emperors.
question.text: This dynasty's emperor Toghon Temur once considered the idea of killing everyone with the surnames Zhang, Wang, Liu, Li, and Zhao, which would've killed more than 90% of China's population. This dynasty was established in China by Kublai Khan.
question.clue: It established its capital at Cambaluc , now modern day Beijing.

swap.text: This economic and social campaign beginning in 1958 sought to rapidly transform China from an agrarian economy to modern communist society. It failed miserably.
swap.clue: This program started with a focus on conserving water before moving to a massive collectivization.

question.text: This military leader of the Kuomintang led the Northern Expedition at the start of the Chinese Civil War. He later led the Republic of China's exiled government on Taiwan.
question.clue: This man was appointed as Commandant of the Whampoa military academy in 1924.

swap.leadin: One quote from this work states "Without an army for the people, there is nothing for the people."
swap.text: Name this work of propaganda, first published in 1964, that praised Marxism and Leninism.
swap.answerHtml: The Little Red Book (accept, but do not reveal, Quotations from Chairman Mao Zedong)
swap.clue: In many "big character posters," workers and soldiers are shown smiling and holding this text high in the air.

question.leadin: Answer the following about your life as a hypothetical Chinese rice farmer in 1977.
question.text: You see Hua Guofeng replaced the following year by this Paramount Leader of China, who instituted market reforms from 1978 to 1992 and put down the Tiananmen Square protests.
question.clue: This "second generation" leader's "Southern Tour" publicized the success of the first four special economic zones he created as part of "reform and opening up."

swap.leadin: A period of the same name in China ended with the establishment of the Qin Dynasty.
swap.text: Identify this time of unrest in Japanese history that began with the Onin War. It resulted in the destruction of Kyoto, the capital of the ruling Ashikaga Shogunate.
swap.clue: Soldiers in an army during this period received tax exemptions for capturing enemy heads; that army was led by a general who supposedly buried 400,000 soldiers alive after a battle during this period.

question.text: The Silla Kingdom allied with this Chinese dynasty to conquer its neighbors. This dynasty was interrupted by Wu Zetian's short-lived Zhou Dynasty.
question.clue: This dynasty lost the battle of Talas to the Abbasids.

swap.leadin: One leader in this conflict rebellion founded the "God Worshipping Society" after repeatedly failing his civil service examinations.
swap.text: Name this rebellion, whose participants primarily belonged to the Hakka and Zhuang ethnic groups. Zeng Guofan created the Hunan Army to suppress this rebellion.
swap.clue: It was further weakened by the desertion of Shih Ta-k'ai, and in 1860, it failed to take Shanghai, which was defended by a force commanded by Frederick Ward.

question.leadin: This man was captured as a youth by imperial forces and castrated when he went by the name of Ma Sanbao.
question.text: Name this Muslim eunuch. He captured King Alagonakkara of Sri Lanka and brought him back to China as a prisoner during one of the seven voyages of his Treasure Fleet.
question.clue: That son, Chenggong, established the "Ming Memorial Prefecture" in southern China.

swap.leadin: This dynasty defeated its predecessor at the Battle of Muye, capturing its capital at modern Anyang.
swap.text: Name this longest ruling Chinese dynasty who thereafter became the first to claim a "Mandate of Heaven" for their rule.
swap.clue: The Hundred Schools flourished during the Eastern part of the dynasty, whose rulers were the first to claim the (* ) Mandate of Heaven.

question.text: This man, Shi Huang-di's Prime Minister, convinced him to order the burning of the books and the burying of a number of Confucian scholars.
question.clue: With the eunuch Zhao Gao, this man forged a letter ordering crown prince Fusu to commit suicide and naming Huhai as the successor to the throne.

swap.text: This city in Shaanxi province was formerly a capital of China called Chang'an. It is home to the Wild Goose Pagoda as well as Qin Shi Huang Di's terra cotta army.
swap.clue: The Silk Road had its eastern origin in this city, where Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi was buried with his Terracotta Army.

question.leadin: Name some things about a Chinese rebellion.
question.text: Led by promises that the Buddha would return, participants in this late eighteenth-century rebellion were ineffectively dealt with by Heshen, who embezzled a lot of the funds that were to be used to put it down.
question.clue: The largest disturbance since the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, this conflict persisted thanks to the staggering greed and stupidity of Heshen, who was finally dismissed after the Jiaqing Emperor replaced the Qianlong Emperor.

swap.leadin: The battle of Xiaoyao Ford during this period raised the reputation of Zhang Liao.
swap.text: Name this period of Chinese history which ended with the defeat of Sun Hao at Jianye. This period was presaged by the Yellow Turban Rebellion.
swap.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

question.text: In 2007, Baumgartner became the first person to BASE jump off of this building, which is named for its number of floors.

swap.leadin: A student at this institution cut off his arm to prove his dedication to his teacher after having stood in the freezing cold all night.
swap.text: Identify this institution where a leader faced a wall for nine years after being initially refused entry. That leader of this institution left some books behind in a chest which his students later found.
swap.clue: Batuo, an Indian, served as this site's first abbot, while this site's apocryphal southern equivalent in Fujian has not been identified.

question.leadin: During its Eastern phase, this dynasty granted tax exemptions to resettled migrants from north China called qiaoren.
question.text: Name this dynasty ruled by the Sima family, whose earlier Western phase began with its reunification of China in 280 CE and ended following multiple civil wars named for Eight Princes and Five Barbarians.
question.clue: Its forces expelled the ruler Yelu Dashi to the west, where he founded the Kara-Khitan Khanate with surviving forces of the Liao dynasty.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Zhou dynasty.
swap.text: You can read about the Spring and Autumn period of the Zhou dynasty in this man's The Spring and Autumn Annals. This historian also authored Shiji and Records of the Grand Historian.
swap.clue: This court eunuch wrote a biography of emperors starting with Huangdi, also known as the Yellow Emperor, to his contemporary Emperor Wu of Han.

question.text: One bolt of silk was equivalent to one tael of silver or one string of these Chinese copper coins, which were circular with a square hole in the middle. Confusingly, the English word for these coins is identical to an unrelated English word for money.
question.clue: A policy that required this stuff replaced the Neutrality Acts in 1939, and was replaced by an act under which the British gave up control of military bases in Bermuda and Newfoundland.

swap.leadin: Many of these things were made using tortoise shells and they were plunged into fires to see how they would crack.
swap.text: Name these objects used in ancient China that people believed showed the future.
swap.clue: Eventually supplanted by the I Ching, these objects were used for divination via plastromancy, scapulimancy, and pyromancy.
